Subject: Hosted API evaluation — quick onramp, endpoint limits & next steps

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great to learn more about ParcelPilot's routing use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps for a Hosted API evaluation: 

Recap (from our call)
- Primary use: high-volume routing decisions during parcel ingestion (avg ~50 tokens / request).
- Desired pilot scope: proof of accuracy + latency under realistic traffic.
- Security items: SOC 2 attestation, IP allowlist, and retention policy questions.

Hosted evaluation offer (what we can provision quickly)
- Quickstart sandbox: test API key + sample workspace to run end-to-end calls. (Attachment: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf)
- Endpoints you will use: POST /v1/generate (streaming supported), POST /v1/embeddings, POST /v1/re-rank.
- Default pilot limits: 600 requests/minute, 10 concurrent streams. We can temporarily raise to a pilot cap (up to 2,000 req/min) on request.
- Token guidance: cost and throttling are per-token; we gave some sample token budgets in the guide.

Action items / next steps
1) Can you share a 48-hour traffic profile (CSV) with sample qps and burst expectations? Even a rough hour-by-hour or synthetic profile helps us size the pilot. (I referenced a CSV template you can fill — feel free to attach it.)
2) Let me know required SLA window for the pilot and any IP ranges to allowlist.
3) Ben (cc) will be available for a technical deep-dive once we have the traffic profile — propose Wed/Thu next week.
4) I can get a temporary elevated rate cap while we run the pilot — confirm target req/min and concurrency.

I attached the quickstart guide to help your engineers get a PoC up and running today. If this all looks good I’ll provision the eval key and a shared test workspace.

Thanks,

— Stephanie Nguyen

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — quick onramp, endpoint limits & next steps

Hi Maya — great, thanks for the profile and latency target. Answers below plus a proposed pilot configuration: 

Answers
- Concurrency & streaming: concurrency is enforced per API key by default. A streaming request counts as one concurrent slot while the connection is open. So 10 concurrent streams means up to 10 long-lived streaming connections per API key; short-lived generate calls count toward the same concurrency pool.
- Rate limits: the 600 req/min baseline is an account-level soft cap for trials; we can provision an elevated pilot cap of 2,000 req/min for up to 14 days with a short request form.
- Throttling behavior: we expose 429 responses with Retry-After; SDKs implement exponential backoff by default.

Proposed pilot config (recommended)
- API key: provisioned for ParcelPilot sandbox, elevated to 1,200 req/min and 25 concurrent streams for first 7 days. We can scale to 2,000 req/min if the profile shows sustained bursts.
- Endpoints: v1/generate for routing, with streaming enabled; v1/embeddings for metadata sync (small batch jobs).
- Observability: we’ll provide a shared dashboard with per-route latency and token breakdowns.

Next steps
1) If you confirm the pilot config above I’ll provision the key and share credentials + allowlist instructions.
2) Ben, can we schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive to discuss batching, prefix caching, and best-practice prompt templates? Suggested slots: Tue 27 Jul 09:00–11:00 PT or Wed 28 Jul 14:00–16:00 PT.
3) If ParcelPilot needs SOC 2 evidence, I’ll attach the report and a short security checklist (I can send that to procurement separately).

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and the IP ranges.

Best,

— Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Maya / Stephanie — looping in product engineering for the tech deep-dive and attaching a short Method-of-Procedure for the pilot. TL;DR of internal plan:

- Provision sandbox API key with 1,200 req/min and 25 concurrent streams for 7 days.
- Monitor for sustained burst >1,800 req/min; if observed, automatically escalate to 2,000 req/min for an additional 7 days.
- Enable prefix caching for routing prompts to reduce token spending and lower latency.
- Observability: share dashboard link after key provisioning.
